title: Bread Tips
desc: Tips and techniques for bread baking
content: bread tips bread tips & recipe guide | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. bread tips & recipe guide your go-to reference for mastering soft, fluffy bread the kind that makes you proud to slice into it. top 10 tips for softer bread 1. increase hydration tip: try increasing the water slightly. a hydration level of around 65% 70% (water weight relative to flour) is ideal. for 570 g of flour, 380 ml gives ~66%. if dough can handle it, add 10 20 ml more water. 2. use the tangzhong (water roux) method what it does: locks in moisture for a super-soft crumb. how to do it: mix 10% of flour ( 57 g) with 5 its weight in water ( 285 ml). heat while stirring until thick, then cool before adding to dough. 3. add more fat tip: 1 2 tbsp butter or olive oil enriches the crumb and flavour. 4. include more dairy tip: 3 4 tbsp full-cream milk powder or replace part of water with whole milk for creamier dough. 5. incorporate eggs tip: one egg (~50 g) adds protein and richness. reduce water by 25 30 ml to balance. 6. adjust rising time tip: don't overproof aim for 80% of maximum rise on the second proof for a good oven spring. 7. add a sweetener tip: 1 2 tbsp honey, sugar, or malt syrup retains moisture and feeds yeast. 8. steam during baking what it does: keeps surface moist for better oven spring. how: tray of hot water on bottom rack or mist oven walls before baking. 9. adjust baking temperature tip: bake at 180 c (355 f) for 30 35 min rather than a long low bake retains moisture. 10. let it cool properly tip: cool on a rack, cover with a clean tea towel to trap gentle steam and soften crust. tangzhong (water roux) method what it does: cooked flour + water/milk mixture retains moisture, giving a soft, fluffy crumb and longer shelf life. ingredients: 57 g bakers flour (~10% of total flour) 285 ml water or milk instructions: whisk flour and water until smooth. heat over medium stirring constantly. mixture thickens to pudding-like consistency (~65 c / 150 f). cool to room temperature before adding to dough. use as part of the liquid in bread e.g., 285 ml in tangzhong + 95 ml in main dough for grain & seed bread. tip can be made ahead and stored in fridge up to 2 days. bring to room temp before use. bread recipes collection 1. classic white bread 570 g bakers flour 345 360 ml water 40 ml olive oil tbsp salt tbsp bread improver tbsp yeast 3 tbsp full-cream powdered milk 1 large egg (70 80 g) optional: 2 tbsp butter or 1 2 tbsp honey 2. grain & seed bread seed/grain mix total 120 g for texture, nutrition, flavour. 510 g bakers flour (reduce if using tangzhong) 285 ml water (tangzhong) + 75 80 ml main dough 40 ml olive oil tbsp salt tbsp bread improver tbsp yeast 120 g seed & grain mix: 15 g rolled oats 10 g brown flaxseed meal 10 g linseed 10 g sesame seeds 10 g white quinoa 10 g black quinoa 5 g black chia 5 g white chia 10 g sunflower seeds 10 g pumpkin kernels 10 g bulgur wheat 10 g whole grain freekeh 5 g poppy seeds 5 g hemp protein powder 5 g hemp seeds 5 g psyllium husk 5 g bran 5 g soy lecithin 3 tbsp full-cream powdered milk 1 large egg (70 80 g) optional: 2 tbsp butter or 1 2 tbsp honey 3. wholemeal bread 570 g wholemeal flour (or part wholemeal + part white for lighter crumb) 345 360 ml water 40 ml olive oil tbsp salt tbsp bread improver (optional) tbsp yeast 3 tbsp full-cream powdered milk 1 large egg (70 80 g) optional: 2 tbsp butter 4. gluten-free bread 400 g gluten-free flour blend 345 360 ml water or milk 40 ml olive oil tbsp salt tbsp yeast 2 3 tbsp full-cream powdered milk 1 2 g xanthan gum 1 large egg (70 80 g) optional: 2 tbsp butter or 1 2 tbsp honey method 1: classic (without tangzhong) mix dry ingredients (flour, salt, bread improver, yeast, milk powder). add wet ingredients (water, olive oil, egg), mix to dough. knead 8 10 min until smooth/elastic. gluten-free: knead until combined. first rise: cover, let double (~1 1.5 hrs). punch down, shape, place in greased tins. second rise: 30 45 min. bake 180 c (350 f) 25 35 min (rolls 18 25 min). gluten-free slightly longer. cool 20 min on wire rack; brush with butter. method 2: tangzhong (with tangzhong) prepare tangzhong: 30 g flour + 150 ml water/milk, cook low heat to paste, cool. mix remaining dry ingredients (flour minus tangzhong flour, salt, bread improver, yeast, milk powder). add wet ingredients (adjusted water, olive oil, egg) + cooled tangzhong, mix to dough. knead 8 10 min until smooth/elastic. gluten-free: knead until combined. first rise: cover, let double (~1 1.5 hrs). punch down, shape, second rise 30 45 min. bake 180 c (350 f) 25 35 min (rolls 18 25 min). gluten-free slightly longer. cool 20 min on wire rack; brush with butter. notes using tangzhong gives softer, fluffier crumb and longer freshness. adjust water slightly depending on flour type and humidity. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print recipe

title: Cheese Sauce Tips
content: cheese sauce tips cheese sauce insights & tips | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. cheese sauce insights & tips everything i've learned about smooth, silky cheese sauces from technique to troubleshooting and personal observations spanning decades. technique tips make a roux first (butter + flour) to stabilise the sauce. add milk slowly while whisking to prevent lumps. add cheese off heat to prevent graininess or oily separation. gradually mix and rewarm gently only if necessary. cheese selection cheddar: classic melt and flavour gruy re: smooth, nutty, traditional french depth parmesan: seasoning boost, sharper flavour mozzarella: stringy, less ideal for smooth sauce australian tasty / mild cheddar: closest to mainland tasty from the 90s why this works the roux stabilises the dairy, preventing separation. slow milk addition prevents lumps. off-heat cheese melt keeps the sauce silky. gradual mixing stops splitting or graininess. common problems & fixes lumps: milk added too fast. fix: whisk hard or use a stick blender. grainy cheese: cheese overheated. fix: add cheese off heat, use gentler-melting cheese. too thick: roux is strong. fix: add more milk gradually. too thin: sauce hasn't thickened. fix: simmer gently to allow starch thickening. personal observations block vs pre-shredded cheese shred block cheese yourself instead of using pre-shredded. that little grain on pre-shredded cheese? i used to wonder what it was hehehe. it took me about 26 years to figure it out! pre-shredded cheese contains anti-caking agents. they prevent sticking but also subtly affect flavour and texture: can make sauce slightly grainy changes melting behaviour and mouthfeel flavour is slightly muted compared to block cheese i've noticed block cheese tastes slightly better than pre-grated. anti-caking agents clearly play a role in flavour. block cheese gives smoother texture, better control, and more authentic taste just like in a professional kitchen. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print notes

title: Culinary Terms
content: culinary terms culinary terms glossary | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. culinary terms glossary here is a comprehensive glossary of 150 key culinary terms, split alphabetically for easy reference. a e al dente: pasta cooked firm to the bite. aioli: garlic-flavored mayonnaise. au jus: meat served with its natural juices. bake: cooking food in an oven using dry heat. baste: brushing or spooning liquid over food while cooking. barding: wrapping meat with fat before cooking. braise: cooking meat slowly in a covered pot with liquid. brine: soaking food in a saltwater solution to season and tenderize. brunoise: finely diced vegetables, usually 1 2 mm. caramelize: cooking sugar or food until it browns. chantilly: sweetened whipped cream. chiffonade: cutting herbs or leafy greens into thin ribbons. chop: cutting food into small pieces. clarify: removing impurities from butter or stock. confit: meat slow-cooked in its own fat. coulis: smooth sauce made from pur ed vegetables or fruit. crumble: breaking ingredients into small pieces. deglaze: adding liquid to a pan to loosen cooked bits. degorge: soaking food to remove excess salt or bitterness. emulsify: mixing two liquids that normally don't combine. f l fillet: removing bones from meat or fish. fold: gently combining ingredients to avoid deflating air. fold-in: gently combining a light mixture into a heavier batter. fry: cooking food in hot oil or fat. ganache: chocolate and cream mixture used as a glaze or filling. glaze: coating food with a glossy finish. grate: shredding food using a grater. gratin: dish topped with breadcrumbs or cheese and browned. grill: cooking food over direct heat. infuse: steeping ingredients in liquid to extract flavor. julienne: cutting food into thin matchstick-sized strips. knead: working dough to develop gluten and elasticity. lard: fat from pork used in cooking and baking. liaison: egg and cream mixture used to thicken sauces. m r macaronage: folding meringue into batter gently. mac doine: diced vegetables or fruit served together. macerate: soaking fruit in liquid, usually with sugar or alcohol. marinate: soaking food in a flavorful liquid before cooking. mise en place: preparing and arranging ingredients before cooking. panade: mixture of bread and liquid used as a binder. pan-fry: cooking food in a small amount of oil over medium heat. parboil: partially boiling food before finishing by another method. parfait: layered dessert with cream and fruit. p te bris e: shortcrust pastry dough. p te sucr e: sweet shortcrust pastry. p t : spread made from ground meat and seasonings. peel: removing skin from fruits or vegetables. pilaf: rice dish cooked in seasoned broth. poach: cooking food gently in simmering liquid. po le: pan-cooked technique. proof: allowing yeast dough to rise before baking. profiterole: small cream-filled pastry. puree: smooth mashed food. quenelle: oval dumpling made from meat or fish paste. reduce: boiling a liquid to thicken and concentrate flavor. render: melting fat from meat. rillette: meat preserved in fat and shredded. risotto: italian rice dish cooked slowly with broth. roquette: peppery salad green (arugula). roast: cooking food in an oven using dry heat. roux: a mixture of fat and flour used to thicken sauces. s z sear: browning the surface of food quickly at high heat. season: adding salt, pepper, or spices to food. shred: cutting food into thin strips. saut : cooking food quickly in a small amount of fat over high heat. simmer: cooking just below boiling point with gentle bubbles. skim: removing impurities or foam from liquids. spatchcock: flattening poultry by removing backbone for even cooking. souffl : light baked dish with whipped egg whites. steam: cooking food with vapor from boiling water. steep: soaking ingredients in liquid to extract flavor. stew: cooking food slowly in liquid for a long time. tempering: slowly heating chocolate or combining hot liquids with eggs. thicken: making a liquid more dense, usually with starch or roux. toss: lightly mixing ingredients together. tourn : cutting vegetables into barrel shapes. velout : white sauce made from stock and roux. vinaigrette: oil and vinegar dressing. whip: beating ingredients to incorporate air and increase volume. whisk: beating ingredients quickly to incorporate air. zest: grated outer skin of citrus fruit for flavor. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print glossary

title: Fact Sheet
content: fact sheet bread hydration & roux: baker's lesson | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. bread hydration & roux: baker's lesson welcome to this comprehensive lesson for bakers. explore dough hydration, high-hydration handling techniques, and roux integration to produce soft, flavorful bread. through theory and practical exercises, gain the skills to plan, mix, and bake breads with predictable texture, structure, and taste. lesson objectives by the end of this lesson, students will be able to: understand dough hydration: predict dough behavior based on water content affecting crumb structure, texture, and handling. calculate hydration percentages: apply formulas to scale recipes accurately for different flour weights. incorporate roux effectively: modify softness, moisture retention, and flavor; adjust hydration accordingly. handle high-hydration dough: use stretch & fold, temperature control, and gentle shaping for wet doughs. plan and execute dough mixes: observe effects of hydration and roux inclusion on dough texture, rise, and final bread quality. tip for students: focus on understanding variables, not just memorizing numbers. observe, adjust, and record results. dough hydration theory dough hydration (%) = (weight of water weight of flour) 100 texture & crumb: higher hydration open, airy crumb; lower hydration tighter crumb. handling: higher hydration stickier dough; use gentle techniques like stretch & fold. crust & oven spring: water turns to steam, improving oven spring and crust. fermentation & flavor: hydration affects yeast activity and enzymatic reactions; higher hydration lighter, complex flavor. example hydration levels (for 590g flour) 65% 384g water: easy to handle, medium crumb. 75% 443g water: softer, slightly open crumb. 85% 502g water: very wet, open crumb; requires stretch & fold and possibly dutch oven. incorporating roux in bread dough roux is a cooked mixture of flour and water (or milk). it enhances: softness: tender crumb that stays soft longer. shelf life: moisture retention keeps bread fresh. flavor: nutty, richer taste. making roux combine flour and water (or milk) in a saucepan. cook over medium heat, stirring until thickened and smooth. cool completely before adding to dough. handling high-hydration dough stretch & fold: strengthens gluten without overworking wet doughs. timing: 3 4 folds at 25 30 min intervals. temperature: use cooler dough if kitchen is warm. handling tips: lightly oil hands and work surface. baking: use preheated dutch oven or covered vessel. hydration trade-off: slightly reducing hydration (e.g., 80%) makes handling easier. observation: learn to judge dough readiness by feel and elasticity. tip for students: observe, record, and adjust hydration and fold technique carefully. practical exercises hydration calculations: scale water for 65%, 75%, 85% hydration for different flour weights. small batch doughs: observe differences in feel, elasticity, and handling challenges. roux experiment: compare 50g roux in 500g flour dough vs control. stretch & fold practice: record folds to achieve windowpane readiness. temperature control: compare ice water vs room-temp water effects. observation & note-taking: track hydration, roux ratios, mixing, and folds for repeatable results. tips & tricks adjust hydration at the start, not mid-rise. add water or roux incrementally when experimenting. include roux water in hydration calculations. reduce hydration slightly for easier handling if needed. keep detailed notes for repeatable results. use ice water to control fermentation temperature. check gluten with windowpane test. stretch & fold gently every 30 minutes. use preheated dutch oven for high-hydration dough. observe dough appearance and elasticity carefully. summary dough hydration: directly affects handling, crumb, and oven spring. high-hydration techniques: stretch & fold, gentle handling, temperature control. roux integration: enhances softness, moisture, flavor. observation & note-taking: essential for reproducible success. hands-on experimentation: small-scale trials refine technique safely. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print lesson

title: Baked Cheesecake
desc: A classic baked cheesecake — rich, smooth, and far more forgiving than its reputation suggests.
content: flavoured cheesecakes flavoured cheesecakes | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. flavoured cheesecakes a versatile no-bake base with endless flavour paths fruity, zesty, or outrageously chocolate-laden. ingredients base 1 packs arnott's nice biscuits, crushed 60 g butter, melted filling base 500 g philadelphia cream cheese sugar to taste (replaces condensed milk) 2 teaspoons gelatin, bloomed flavour options mango: blend fresh mango into the filling and top with sliced mango. passionfruit: stir in passionfruit pulp (john's favourite) and finish with fresh pulp. strawberry: puree strawberries for the mix and add sliced berries on top. lemon: add fresh lemon juice and zest for a bright, clean flavour. chocolate bars: melt and mix in: mars bar toblerone ferrero rocher turkish delight add chopped pieces on top for texture. method combine crushed nice biscuits with melted butter, then press firmly into your pan. blend philadelphia cream cheese, sugar, and your chosen flavour ingredient until smooth. add the dissolved gelatin and mix until completely combined. pour over the base and chill 4 6 hours or overnight. decorate just before serving. flavour notes for extra intensity: reduce fruits slightly on the stove to concentrate their flavour before mixing in. chocolate variations set firmer, so keep the gelatin amount the same. helpful reminder if your recipe uses gelatine especially cold-set cheesecakes here's the guide that shows you exactly how to bloom it properly: gelatine blooming guide 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print recipe

title: Gelatin Blooming Guide
desc: How to bloom and use gelatin correctly
content: gelatin blooming guide how to bloom gelatin | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. how to bloom gelatin a simple but essential technique for smooth, lump-free cold-set cheesecakes. treat gelatin right, and it will reward you with a perfect, velvety set. steps measure out 2 teaspoons powdered gelatin . sprinkle evenly over cup cold water or fruit juice . let stand for 5 10 minutes until thick and spongy. gently heat about 10 15 seconds in the microwave or over a warm pan just until fully dissolved. let it cool slightly, then fold into your cheesecake mixture. pro tips never add dry gelatin straight into hot mixtures it clumps like a toddler with play-doh. don't boil it; gentle heat keeps it behaving. fruit juice adds flavour that ties your cheesecake together beautifully. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print guide

title: Tangzhong Guide
desc: Complete guide to the tangzhong method
content: tangzhong guide tangzhong guide | ajpc kitchen notebook print option available at the bottom of the page. tangzhong guide a complete guide to making tangzhong, scaling it, adjusting the roux, using corn flour, and gluten-free alternatives. includes methods for stove, electric frypan, and microwave. 1. basic tangzhong 30 g wheat flour (taken from total dough flour) 190 g water (accounts for evaporation during cooking) ratio: roughly 1 part flour : 6 parts water (wetter style). storage: cool completely, store airtight in fridge for 3 4 days. bring to room temperature before adding to dough. 2. scaling tangzhong quadruple batch: 120 g flour + 760 g water yields ~880 g tangzhong (less than 1 liter) half batch: 15 g flour + 95 g water yields ~110 g tangzhong 3. increasing roux for softer bread example 1.5 roux: 50 g flour + 315 g water tip: reduce extra water or add a little flour in the main dough to keep it manageable. 4. using corn flour instead of wheat flour thickens faster than wheat flour no gluten contribution structure depends on main dough flour gives a custard-like crumb conversion example: original wheat tangzhong: 30 g flour + 190 g water corn flour version: 10 12 g corn flour + 190 g water cook gently until thickened, then cool before adding to dough. hybrid option: combine half wheat, half corn flour for extra softness without gumminess. 5. gluten-free tangzhong using buckwheat, rice flour, and tapioca starch: buckwheat flour: ~30 40% of flour, adds flavor and color, heavier texture rice flour: ~40 50%, high starch, thickens well tapioca starch: ~10 20%, very starchy, adds chewiness (too much gummy) example batch: 15 g buckwheat flour 15 g rice flour 5 g tapioca starch 190 g water cook gently until thickened, stir constantly, then cool before adding to dough. tip: use binders like xanthan gum or psyllium husk in the main dough; tangzhong improves moisture but won't provide elasticity. 6. cooking methods for tangzhong stove method (preferred) mix flour and water in a small saucepan. cook over low-medium heat, stirring constantly. remove when it thickly coats the back of a spoon but is still pourable. cool before adding to dough. electric frypan method use a small frypan with temperature control if possible. combine flour and water, stir constantly to avoid sticking. heat until lightly thickened; stop just before it becomes stiff. cool before adding to dough. microwave method mix flour and water in a microwave-safe bowl. microwave at medium power for 20 30 seconds at a time, stirring after each interval. repeat until it coats the back of a spoon but is still pourable. cool completely before adding to dough. overcooking warning: tangzhong that becomes very thick, stiff, or gluey has been overcooked. slightly thinner than desired is safer; it will thicken as it cools. 7. quick reference: tangzhong amounts approximate tangzhong amounts for 1 standard loaf (~500 g flour) depending on flour type: flour type flour in tangzhong water in tangzhong notes wheat flour 30 g 190 g classic tangzhong; covers ~1 loaf wheat + corn flour hybrid 15 g wheat + 10 g corn 190 g gives custardy, soft crumb gluten-free (buckwheat + rice + tapioca) 15 g buckwheat + 15 g rice + 5 g tapioca 190 g use binders in dough; keeps crumb moist 1.5 larger loaf (wheat) 50 g 315 g extra roux for softer bread tip: always cool tangzhong before adding to dough; adjust water slightly if making smaller or larger batches. 2026 ajpc | kian tayo | all rights reserved. print guide
